sub_site: pan-cancer SRA re-analysis; eligible types extracted: brain, breast, endometrial, liver, lung, lymphoma, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, thyroid tumours (+ adjacent normal)

data_source.dataset: NCBI SRA (94 projects; RNA-seq/WGS/WES of tumour and adjacent normal tissue)

evidence.quote: We collected a total of 7104 samples from 94 projects in the NCBI SRA database
the data came from the sequencing data of RNA-seq, WGS and WES
were classified as microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, and archaea) identified by kraken2

decontamination.tool: Poore et al. contaminant blacklists + mbodymap whitelist (Ombodymap)

evidence.quote: We referred to Poore et al. from four levels to determine the ‘blacklists’.
Therefore, this study will be based on filtered data5: ‘Ombodymap’ for further exploration.

notes: Kraken2 on SRA host sequencing data, 15 cancers; only genera tied to eligible tumour types recorded (excluded: Faecalibacterium, Hymenobacter, Rhodopseudomonas, Thioalkalivibrio, Helicobacter - only colorectal/gastric/oesophageal/cervical). Table 2 genus names appear only in the first row of each block, so Bacteroides (prostate/thyroid) and Herbaspirillum (lung) are cited to the first row (colorectal). Bacillus/Pasteurella/Mycolicibacterium are top 3 across all 15 types pooled. Synechococcus is a hub in adjacent-normal networks of lymphoma/prostate. n = tumour + adjacent samples of eligible types from Table 1.
